title: Skill assessment of three earth system models with common marine biogeochemistry
problem: Comparing ocean biogeochemistry in Earth system models is challenging because their multiple differences in resolution and physics make it difficult to disentangle whether simulation errors arise from the physical ocean circulation model or from the biogeochemical component itself.
method: The paper assesses three Earth system models by implementing a common ocean biogeochemical model (PISCES) to isolate and evaluate how differences in atmospheric components, ocean physics, and resolution impact the simulation of marine biogeochemistry.
task: The task is to assess the skill of three distinct Earth system models, which share a common marine biogeochemistry component, by comparing their simulations of ocean physics and biogeochemical fields against modern observational data.

innovation: This paper assesses three Earth system models with a common biogeochemistry module, attributing improved upper-ocean biogeochemical skill in newer models to better surface physics, while linking their degraded deep-ocean skill to a poorer representation of deep circulation compared to the older model.

The oceanic component of IPSL-CM5A-LR is based on the ocean part of the 'Nucleus for European Modelling of the Ocean' (NEMOv3.2, Madec 2008a, b). It has a horizontal resolution of 2°-0.5° at the Equator and 31 vertical levels. NEMOv3.2 also includes the sea ice model LIM2 (Fichefet and Maqueda 1997), and the marine biogeochemistry model PISCES. NEMOv3.2 uses a partial-step formulation (Barnier et al. 2006), which improves the representation of bottom bathymetry and thus water flow and effects of friction at the bottom of the ocean.

Compared to the parametrizations of the mixed-layer dynamics used in OPA8, those used in NEMOv3.2 accounts accounts for a double diffusion process (Merryfield et al. 1999), Langmuir cell (Axell 2002), and the contribution of surface wave breaking (Mellor and Blumberg 2004; Burchard and Rennau 2008).

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: It also includes a parameterization of bottom intensified tidal-driven mixing, similar to Simmons et al. (2004), in combination with a specific tidal mixing parameterization in the Indonesian area (Koch-Larrouy et al. 2007, 2010).
The ocean component also uses NEMOv3.2 but in the ORCA1 configuration (Hewitt et al. 2011).

In ORCA1, a nominal resolution of 1° at the equator is chosen to which a latitudinal grid refinement of 1/3° is added in the tropics. The vertical discretization accounts for 42 levels and also includes partial-steps.
Compared to IPSLCM5, this configuration includes an improvement of the Turbulent Kinetic Energy closure scheme (Madec 2008a, b) from Blanke and Delecluse (1993).
